messages.subject: Finding genes in the first & second principal components
messages.subject_clean: Finding genes in the first & second principal components
messages.body_plain:
Good Day Dr. Altuna,  I have 2 questions regarding the PCA function in your methyl-kit package

1- Regarding the function itself: can I peek to the PCA like the function summary with prcomp r function ? how I can manipulate the plots ?
I have read the documentation of PCASamples() function and I see it is based on prcomp and accept methylation percentage matrix,
so I generated the matrix using the function mat=percMethylation() and tried to use prcomp directly but it didn't work, did I miss something?

mat=percMethylation(meth)
prcomp(mat, scale = TRUE)
plot(prcomp(mat))
summary(prcomp(mat))
biplot(prcomp(mat, scale = TRUE))

2- is regarding general approach advise, I have generated the plots below, as you can see both PCA analysis and clustering produced perfect separation between the Rat tissue types.
In the next steps, I want to isolates regions in PC1 and PC2 which contributed the most to this separation, then I want to categorize them, tissue specific genes,  genes promoters, islands, enhancer, etc. I’m guessing I need to used genmoation package but I cannot link it to my PCA results, I only know how to annotate the DMRs like described in the tutorial.
PS. my Data is single based resolution (~1.5 m CpG) from agilent sureselect targeted enriched system (not Whole genome RBSS).

my code is below

#--------------loading------------

library(TxDb.Rnorvegicus.UCSC.rn4.ensGene)

library(genomation)

library(dplyr)

library(GenomicRanges)

library(methylKit)

library(foreach)

library(doMC)

registerDoMC(20)

#####-------reading----------##############

ids = c(

 "blood_1" ,

 "blood_2",

 "cortex_1",

 "cortex_2",

 "hippo_f_1" ,

 "hippo_f_2",

 "hippo_f_3" ,

 "hippo_f_4." ,

 "hippo_m_1",

 "hippo_m_2" ,

 "hippo_m_3",

 "hippo_m_4",

 "hypoth_1",

 "hypoth_2",

 "liver_1",

 "liver_2"

)

# f <- list.files(pattern = "replicat")

# read methylRaw objects to a list in parallel

#--------------------------- for Each loop

allSamples <- foreach(i = 1:length(f)) %dopar%

 methRead(

 f[[i]],

 sample.id = ids[i],

 assembly = "rn4",

 pipeline = list(

 # how is your data files structred

 fraction = TRUE,

 chr.col = 1,

 start.col = 2,

 end.col = 2,

 coverage.col = 6,

 strand.col = 4,

 freqC.col = 5

 ),treatment = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4)

 )

# make a new methylRawList object from the list

myobj = new("methylRawList",

 allSamples,

 treatment = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4))

filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(myobj,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL,

 hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

for (i in 1:16){

 getCoverageStats(filtered.myobj[[i]],plot=TRUE,both.strands=FALSE)

}

######----PCA--------#######

meth=unite(filtered.myobj, destrand=FALSE)

head(meth)

clusterSamples(meth, dist="correlation", method="ward", plot=TRUE)

PCASamples(meth, screeplot=TRUE)

messages.subject: Invalid input file format for methylInheritance
messages.subject_clean: Invalid input file format for methylInheritance
messages.body_plain:
Our goal is to use the permutation test from methylInheritance (runObservation and runPermutation methods) between 2 environments with RRBS data.

We used the BAM files from bismark to get methylation calls for individuals using the processBismarkAln method, as [1]. This generated the CpG text files for each individual, as expected.

After that, we used the methRead method to get the methylRawList object, which is the input for the methylInheritance method. The methRead command, as [2], is referencing the CpG files from the previous step. We tried both separating and putting together different generations (we have two). However, the output of the methRead command is not returning a methylRawList object, it is generating a methylRaw object instead. This is causing the error "methylkit data must be a list containing "methyl RawList" entries; each entry must contain all "methylRaw" objects related to one generation" in the methylInheritance method, as [3].

Also, we realised that the methylRaw object has been generated with all positions, instead  of the shared ones across all individuals. After checking the manual, we thought we could use unite(), as [4], in methylKit to merge the common positions, however it outputs a methylBase object, which we cannot input in methylInheritance and we don't  know how to transform into a methylRawList object.

We appreciate any help.
